native_result.query: At what Socioeconomic levels is the advantage in completion rates for Black students more pronounced?
native_result.HypoA: The advantage in BA degree completion rates for Black students becomes more pronounced at higher SES levels indicated by a positive interaction term SES*is_Black(coefficient:0.6271 (significant))
native_result.HypoB: Преимущество Black студентов в завершении BA над White проявляется только на самых высоких уровнях SES: в верхней квартили SES (SES > 0.41) разрыв с White сокращается до −0.6 п.п. и статистически неотличим от нуля, а после контроля способности (ASVAB), классного процентиля и пола появляется небольшое положительное преимущество Black в верхней половине SES (≈ +1.2 п.п., взаимодействие Black×высокий-SES p≈0.06). Ни на одном более низком уровне SES преимущества нет — наоборот, зафиксирован дефицит, максимальный в нижней-средней квартили (Q2: 1.3% vs 4.3% у White, −3.0 п.п., 95% ДИ [−4.4;−1.4]); паттерн устойчив к разбиению на 3 полосы SES.
native_result.WorkflowB: Дескриптивная стратификация по квартилям SES (единые границы): доли BA DEGREE COMPLETED=1 по расам, разности долей Black−White и Hispanic−White в п.п. с ДИ Newcombe и точным тестом Фишера; чувствительность — 3 полосы SES и логистическая регрессия BA ~ Black×SES + пол + ABILITY + процентиль (и пополовинам SES). Код: analysis/nls_ses_analysis.py.

sub_hypo.text: The advantage in BA degree completion rates for Black students becomes more pronounced at higher SES levels, indicated by a significant positive SES × is_Black interaction coefficient of 0.6271.
sub_hypo.context: NLS participants with social background factors and academic resources recorded at the time of secondary school graduation.
sub_hypo.relations: The advantage in BA degree completion rates for Black students increases as SES rises, with a significant positive interaction between SES and Black race status (coefficient: 0.6271).

gold_sub_hypo.full_hypo: The advantage in BA degree completion rates for Black students becomes more pronounced at higher SES levels indicated by a positive interaction term SES*is_Black(coefficient:0.6271 (significant))

sub_hypo.text: Among NLS participants in the highest SES quartile (SES > 0.41), the Black–White gap in BA completion narrows to −0.6 percentage points and is statistically indistinguishable from zero.
sub_hypo.context: Black and White NLS participants in the highest SES quartile, using common SES quartile boundaries (SES > 0.41).
sub_hypo.relations: The Black-minus-White BA completion difference is −0.6 percentage points in the highest SES quartile and is not statistically distinguishable from zero.

sub_hypo.text: After controlling for ASVAB ability, class percentile, and sex, Black participants show a small positive BA completion advantage over White participants in the upper half of SES, approximately +1.2 percentage points, with Black×high-SES interaction p≈0.06.
sub_hypo.context: Black and White NLS participants, comparing SES halves and adjusting for ability, class percentile, and sex.
sub_hypo.relations: SES moderates the adjusted relationship between race and BA completion: the Black-minus-White difference becomes approximately +1.2 percentage points in the upper SES half; the Black×high-SES interaction has p≈0.06.

sub_hypo.text: At lower SES levels, Black participants have no BA completion advantage over White participants; instead, they show a deficit, largest in the lower-middle SES quartile (Q2), where completion rates are 1.3% versus 4.3%, a difference of −3.0 percentage points with a 95% confidence interval of [−4.4, −1.4].
sub_hypo.context: Black and White NLS participants at lower SES levels, stratified by common SES quartile boundaries, particularly the lower-middle quartile (Q2).
sub_hypo.relations: Black BA completion rates are below White rates at lower SES levels. The largest deficit occurs in Q2: 1.3% versus 4.3%, with a Black-minus-White difference of −3.0 percentage points and 95% CI [−4.4, −1.4].

sub_hypo.text: The SES-dependent pattern in Black–White BA completion differences remains robust when SES is divided into three bands rather than quartiles.
sub_hypo.context: Black and White NLS participants, with sensitivity analysis using three SES bands instead of quartiles.
sub_hypo.relations: The pattern of Black BA completion deficits at lower SES and a narrowing gap at the highest SES persists under three-band SES stratification.

gen_sub_hypo.full_hypo: Преимущество Black студентов в завершении BA над White проявляется только на самых высоких уровнях SES: в верхней квартили SES (SES > 0.41) разрыв с White сокращается до −0.6 п.п. и статистически неотличим от нуля, а после контроля способности (ASVAB), классного процентиля и пола появляется небольшое положительное преимущество Black в верхней половине SES (≈ +1.2 п.п., взаимодействие Black×высокий-SES p≈0.06). Ни на одном более низком уровне SES преимущества нет — наоборот, зафиксирован дефицит, максимальный в нижней-средней квартили (Q2: 1.3% vs 4.3% у White, −3.0 п.п., 95% ДИ [−4.4;−1.4]); паттерн устойчив к разбиению на 3 полосы SES.
